Founders

India needs people who start companies.

Start by building something real. The founder path takes you from finding a problem to testing a pilot with customers, with engineering and management students working side by side.

Book a campus visit

From a real problem to a first customer

Year 1 · Find a problem

Look for problems worth solving in factories, farms, hospitals and small businesses.

Year 2 · Build for one user

Pick a named user, build for them and speak with people who might buy the product.

Year 3 · Run a pilot

Build a small batch, put it in users’ hands and see what they use and what they would pay for.

Year 4 · Develop a venture

The proposed final-semester founder route focuses on a working product, a customer or pilot, and a plan to make and deliver it.

Build with people who have different skills

The programme brings together students from four engineering courses and from the BBA and MBA. The founder path is designed around access to Factory tools, guidance from engineers and entrepreneurs, and help navigating government startup schemes.

The same projects and practical skills also prepare students who choose to join an established company.

Explore the management courses

For those who want the detail

A founder team must demonstrate a working product, a real customer or pilot, and a credible plan to produce and deliver it. Final-semester credit for startup work depends on the university’s academic regulations.

An on-campus incubator, small prototype grants and internships offered by graduate-founded companies are planned initiatives. Their availability depends on programme decisions.
